title: fix(cli): os lint and os i18n check expect a contributed navigation item's label under its target app
body:
Fixes #24993

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

`collectExpectedEntries` (`packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`) is the one walk behind `os lint`'s `i18n/missing-*` family, `os i18n check` and `os i18n extract`. Its navigation arm read `apps[].navigation` only. An item a package contributes into an app through `manifest.navigationContributions` (ADR-0029 D7) never enters that array: the runtime folds it in on every read (`SchemaRegistry.applyNavContributions`), and `translateApp` resolves its label from `apps.TARGET.navigation.ID.label`. `translation-target-unknown` accepts that key since #18203. So the key was accepted but never expected, and deleting its translation left both doors green.

- **New arm.** After the apps' own trees, every `navigationContributions[]` entry is walked by the same `walkNavigation`, keyed under its target `app`. The seed is the item's own `label`. A contributed group's children follow the rule an own group's children follow. An entry with no string `app` is skipped.
- **Carriers.** `navigationContributionsOf` reads the two carriers the target rule reads (`contributedNavItemsByApp` in `packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts`): the stack's own `manifest.navigationContributions`, and `packages[].manifest.navigationContributions` (the ADR-0130 D4 entry body). Both are read unconditionally, as the rule reads them. On a `preserve` composition whose last input is the contributor, both carriers hold the same items, and the walker's existing `dedupeByPath` keeps one entry per key (first emission wins, so an id an app also declares keeps the app's own entry).
- **Unchanged.** An app's own items: same walk, same order, emitted first. `i18n-coverage.ts` is not touched: its surface phrase already reads "navigation items".
- Changeset `.changeset/24993-contributed-nav-i18n-coverage.md`: `@objectstack/cli` `patch`.

## The mechanism hypotheses, measured (BASE `6b44efa7b`)

- **H1: confirmed in shape; reuse not taken.** The arm adds each `navigationContributions[].items[]` id under its target app's `navigation` keys. The target rule's resolution is `contributedNavItemsByApp`, which is module-private to `@objectstack/lint` (its index exports `validateTranslationReferences`, not the reader). Importing it would need a new public export from `@objectstack/lint`, outside this card's file surface. The other in-repo readers each need a new import line in `i18n-extract.ts`'s import block, which the dispatch reserved for PR #24947: `collectNavGroupInputs` (cli) reads either/or carriers, not both; `stackPackageBodies` (`@objectstack/core`) covers only the package carrier. So the carrier read is written here, in about ten lines that mirror the rule's two carriers. It is held to the rule by a parity pin, described below.
- **H2: confirmed.** The seed label is the contributed item's own `label` (`sourceValue` / `inline` = `Cases`). The key sits under the app it is contributed TO, read from every package body of the composed artifact (the union stack both doors hand the walker since #22238).
- **H3: confirmed.** A contributed group (`grp_knowledge`) and its child (`nav_article`) are both expected, by the same `walkNavigation` the own tree uses. Deleting the child's key is reported.
- **H4: refuted as a coverage move.** `examples/app-multi-package` contributes `nav_orders` into `multi_crm`, but it declares no `i18n` block and ships no bundle. Only the default locale is active, and its inline labels satisfy it. Its `check:i18n-coverage` count stays at its baselined `0`. No example declares a translated locale and also contributes navigation, so there was nothing to translate and no baseline moved.

## Both doors, measured on the card's probe

The fixture has the card's shape: a service module contributes `nav_case` into the app's `grp_service` group, and adds a group of its own (`grp_knowledge` with child `nav_article`). It is composed module-first with `manifest: 'preserve'`, so the contributions live only in the module's package body. The fixture declares `en` and `zh-CN`, and every other key is translated. Each row deletes one zh-CN navigation key. Run with the source CLI (`bin/run-dev.js`) from a scratch directory, at `d4e0e405a`. The ablated runs used the same tree with the arm's loop emptied, as in the ablation below.

| zh-CN key deleted | `os lint --strict --json`, fixed | ablated (arm removed) | `os i18n check --json --strict`, fixed | ablated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | exit 0, `failing: 0` | exit 0 | exit 0, 15 keys expected | exit 0, 12 keys expected |
| `nav_case` (contributed) | **exit 1**, `i18n/missing-navigation` `translations.zh-CN.apps.cnv_desk.navigation.nav_case.label` | exit 0, no finding | **exit 1**, `error zh-CN apps.cnv_desk.navigation.nav_case.label` | exit 0, no finding |
| `nav_article` (child of a contributed group) | **exit 1**, same rule, `…nav_article.label` | exit 0, no finding | **exit 1**, `…nav_article.label` | exit 0, no finding |
| `nav_accounts` (control: the app's own) | exit 1, `…nav_accounts.label` | exit 1, `…nav_accounts.label` | exit 1 | exit 1 |

The ablated column reproduces the card's finding: the contributed deletions exit 0, and the own-item control exits 1.

## Tests

New `packages/cli/test/i18n-contributed-nav-coverage.test.ts` (unit tier: no spawn, no kernel). It has 13 cases over the real `defineStack` + `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` + `authoringRuleUnionStack` path that both doors take:

- **The walker.** It expects each contributed item under the target app, after the app's own items, seeded with its own label. It reads a single stack's own manifest, including for an app the stack only contributes into. When the top-level manifest is the contributor's copy, each key is expected once. An own id reused by a contribution keeps the app's entry.
- **The gate.** With every label translated, there is no navigation gap. A deleted contributed item is reported, and so is a deleted child of a contributed group. The own-item control is reported as before. When both carriers hold the contribution, the deleted key is reported once.
- **Parity with `translation-target-unknown`.** A zh-CN bundle carrying exactly the navigation keys the walker expects draws no `translation-target-unknown` finding, on the composed stack and on a contribute-only single stack. Each case first asserts that the bundle really carries the contributed ids, so the pin cannot pass empty. The control: an id nothing declares or contributes is still refused.

**Ablation.** The fix was committed first. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the arm's `for (const contribution of navigationContributionsOf(config)) {` with a loop over `[]`. The tool reported the anchor going 1 → 0 and the blob `c23f3ab341d6` → `055daea8a714`. The test file and the subject resolve from `src/` (relative import; `run-dev.js` runs `src/` through tsx), so no `dist/` leg applies.

- Ablated: **8 failed | 5 passed (13)**. All 8 contributed-specific cases went red. The 5 that stayed green are the controls: the fixture shape, the own-id dedupe, no gap when every label is translated, the own-item report, and the ghost-id refusal.
- Restored: blob == HEAD (`c23f3ab341d6`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty (the tool's own verdict).
- Fixed: **13 passed (13)**.

## Local verification

Final head `4f263166d`: this branch plus a merge of `main` at `06900c9c2`, which brought one objectui pin bump and touches no file of this diff. Every lock run below printed its own VERDICT line, which is quoted.

- **Typecheck.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`) → `VERDICT command-exit 0`, test-layer debt held at 3 files / 28 errors / 6 pinned signatures. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test file once, so it is type-checked.
- **Unit tier.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2` at `0c16d8246` (before the merge) → **Test Files 323 passed (323) · Tests 4769 passed (4769)**, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The integration tier is left to CI: this diff touches no spawn entry and no integration-tier file.
- **Re-check after the merge, at `4f263166d`.** The new file, plus the three cli tests that read `.objectui-sha`: **4 files, 44 tests passed**.
- **Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 68 commands. All 68 were run at `4f263166d`, with each exit code captured before any pipe. `--ran`: `68 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 66 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED`, 0 unrun. Readings that bear on this change:
  - `check:i18n-coverage`: `OK (14 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`. The first attempt refused with exit 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (the showcase example's `connector-slack` was unbuilt). The re-run came after the gate's own printed turbo build.
  - `check:i18n`: `OK (10 package(s) — all bundles in sync`.
  - `check:i18n-walk-parity`: `11 declared group(s), 9 walked, 2 exempted`.
  - `check:test-source-alias`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:issue-citations` and `check:doc-authoring`: green.
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:type-check-debt`.** Reason: twice `VERDICT queue-timeout (exit 99)`. The shared verify lock was held more than 19 minutes by another session's `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` (pid 28810, alive). CI's required jobs run it.
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`.** Reason: `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, because six packages outside this diff's closure have no `dist/` (`studio`, `client-react`, `embedder-openai`, `knowledge-ragflow`, `organizations`, `service-cluster-redis`). The build that would supply them got the same queue-timeout. CI's required jobs run it.
- **Dogfood.** Not run: the title carries no `!` and `Clause-②` has no `(narrowing)` arm.

## Acceptance notes

- **A module cannot ship a contributed item's translation without restating the target app's label.** In `TranslationDataSchema`, the `apps.APP` entry requires `label` (`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`). Measured: a module pack carrying only `apps.cnv_desk.navigation.nav_case.label` is refused by `defineStack` with `translations.0.zh-CN.apps.cnv_desk.label: Required property 'label' is missing.` That refusal is loud, not silent. The way around it is to restate the label of an app the module does not own, and that restated label merges with the owner's translation. Whether the module's copy then wins at runtime is not measured. This is a boundary note, not filed. The fixture keeps every navigation label in the app package's pack, the layout HotCRM's packs were measured in (#18203). Carrier: none.
- **The walker and the target rule still walk an item differently.** The walker reads `id ?? name` and descends `items` as well as `children`. The rule reads `id` and descends `children` only, plus `areas[].navigation`, which `translateApp` does not translate. For own items this predates this PR and is unchanged. On spec-valid input (an `id` and `children`) the two agree, and the parity pin holds them there. Noted, not filed. Carrier: none.
